## Incident Report — StrRAT Infection on DESKTOP-SKBR25F

**Evidence:** `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (11,562 packets, 2024-07-30 06:38:48–06:48:34). No IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence folder; findings are derived solely from packet analysis with tshark.

### Victim host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.16.1.66 |
| MAC address | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F |
| AD domain | WIRESHARKWORKSH / wiresharkworkshop.online (DC: WIRESHARK-WS-DC, 172.16.1.4) |
| Logged-in user | **ccollier** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString and inside the malware's own beacon payload) |

### Malware family
**StrRAT** (Java-based remote access trojan), reported client version **1.6**. Attribution is **signature-confirmed**, not behavioral: the malware's own beacon protocol contains the literal ASCII string `STRRAT` in every check-in, which is StrRAT's well-documented, hardcoded pipe-delimited ping format.

### C2 beacon evidence (stream, tcp.stream eq 83)
- First SYN: frame 9066, **2024-07-30 06:40:05 (+04:00)**, `172.16.1.66:49754 → 141.98.10.79:12132`
- Plaintext (non-TLS) TCP, sent roughly every 5 seconds for the remainder of the capture (~508 s duration).
- Decoded beacon body (pipe-delimited):
  ```
  ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender|<base64 active-window-title>|1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime>
  ```
  - Campaign/build ID: `1BE8292C`
  - Base64 field decodes to the active window title, e.g. `UHJvZ3JhbSBNYW5hZ2Vy` = "Program Manager"
  - "Not Installed" corresponds to StrRAT's VM/sandbox-detection field
  - "Sec"/"min...sec" fields show live uptime counters (4 min 25 sec ... 5 min 10 sec across the beacons observed), confirming an active, persistent implant rather than a one-off connection.
- No DNS lookup for 141.98.10.79 appears anywhere in the capture — the implant is hardcoded to connect directly to the IP, no domain fronting observed.

### Indicators of Compromise
| Type | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | **141.98.10.79:12132** | Plaintext TCP, StrRAT ping protocol, persistent throughout capture |
| Malicious domain(s) | None observed | C2 used raw IP:port only; no DNS resolution for the C2 IP found in the capture |
| Malicious URL(s) | None observed | No cleartext HTTP request carried a payload; only benign `connecttest.txt` (Microsoft NCSI) and `ip-api.com/json/` (geolocation lookup — consistent with malware/host doing an IP/geo self-check, response showed public IP 136.49.34.127, Austin, TX, US) were seen in HTTP |
| Transferred file names / SHA256 | **Not observable in this capture** | No file transfer or executable/jar delivery appears in cleartext anywhere in the pcap. TLS sessions to github.com / objects.githubusercontent.com (140.82.113.3, 185.199.110.133) and javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com carried the largest byte volumes in the capture and are the most likely delivery/dependency channels (GitHub-hosted payload staging, Java runtime download), but their contents are TLS-encrypted and cannot be extracted without session keys — do not have grounds to state a specific filename or hash |

### Summary
DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as domain user `ccollier` on the wiresharkworkshop.online AD domain, is running an active StrRAT v1.6 implant (build ID 1BE8292C) beaconing every ~5 seconds in cleartext to 141.98.10.79:12132 starting at 06:40:05. Attribution is confirmed by the malware's self-identifying `STRRAT` string embedded in its own C2 protocol, not by heuristic/behavioral inference. Initial-access vector and any dropped payload (filename/hash) cannot be determined from this capture alone — the largest data transfers in the trace (to github.com/githubusercontent.com and oracle.com) are TLS-encrypted and did not yield recoverable file artifacts.
